Hi Alex / Sanjay,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Wanted to summarize the key SLO/ops items we captured and confirm next steps so we can scope the dedicated routing/edge strategy for Finova.

Call recap (high level):
- Workload: customer-facing chat agent + high-volume embeddings for search/rerank.
- Latency targets: interactive chat (streaming responses) --> p95 <= 200ms token latency (end-to-end for user-visible tokens), p99 <= 500ms; embeddings/rerank batch requests can tolerate higher latencies.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 200 req/s for chat (burstable to 500 req/s), sustained concurrency target ~50 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: MUST support streaming responses (chunked token stream over long-lived connection).
- Regional routing / residency: EU users must have EU data residency for both inference and logging/audit artifacts (cannot leave EU). US primary region for North American users; APAC support preferred with slightly relaxed latency SLOs.
- Fallbacks: prefer automatic fallback to smaller-quantized models in case of capacity pressure, with explicit QoS controls so core customers not impacted.

Open questions we flagged:
1) Exact distribution of traffic by region (approx % US/EU/APAC) — you said you'd share expected volumes per geography.
2) Are audit logs and request payloads subject to retention rules beyond 90 days in EU? (legal asked about 7-year retention for certain records).
3) Any strict egress restrictions for EU that would prevent us from sending telemetry to our US control plane?

Attachments: I attached the SLO template we discussed (finova_slo_requirements.xlsx) and the sample network trace you shared during debug (network_trace_sample.pcap).

Next steps:
- Action (Finova): share regional traffic split + any regulatory retention constraints (Alex).
- Action (Redwood): Neha to run a technical deep-dive on streaming concurrency and KV-cache behavior; we'll propose a routing plan (regional pinning + failover) and a cost estimate for Dedicated capacity vs Hosted with private regional endpoints.
- Schedule: propose Wed Feb 25 for the deep-dive (30–45min).

I'll follow up with a calendar invite once Alex confirms.

Thanks,

Marissa — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Regional traffic split (estimates): US 65%, EU 30%, APAC 5% (expected to grow to ~12% APAC in next 12 months).
- Retention: EU audit logs must be retained for at least 3 years for financial records; certain traces may need up to 7 years. We need a solution that can keep EU-resident logs without egress to US.
- Streaming concurrency: the concurrency number you picked looks right; we also need per-tenant throttles so our premium customers get reserved lanes.

Two technical asks for the deep-dive:
1) How does Redwood handle prefix/KV cache across regionally routed requests — is the cache per-region or global (we need EU isolation).
2) On fallback models: when you auto-fallback to a quantized model, what's the observed p95 delta for streaming token throughput (and any implications for hallucination rates)?

We'll confirm Wed Feb 25 morning PT (aiming for 9:30am PT). Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Hi Alex — quick technical notes before the deep-dive so we can target the session: 

1) KV/prefix cache: we can operate caches per-region (and per-customer within a region) to meet EU isolation requirements. Cache metadata and cold-warm migration can be confined to EU-only hardware. That said, cross-region cache warming is possible if you allow it.

2) Streaming behavior & p95 delta on fallback: in our internal benchmarks, falling back from 16-bit float model to an 8-bit quantized variant typically adds ~20–40ms p95 token latency under light load; under high concurrency the delta increases (depends on kernel availability). For streaming token rate, throughput per connection is usually similar — the main trade is slightly higher compute time per token and small regressions in certain rare long-tail generations. We'll include specific microbenchmarks for Finova's model family in the deep-dive.

3) Per-tenant QoS: we support weighted routing + reserved capacity pools in Dedicated; for Hosted we can create isolated pools per-tenant in dedicated regions (requires reserved commit).

4) Logs & telemetry: we can keep inference logs and traces resident in EU and ship aggregated, non-PII telemetry to our control plane; for full-fidelity logs retained >1yr we can provision EU-only storage buckets and export mechanisms.

I'll bring kernel-selection and quantization microbench slides to the deep-dive.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
